statement: MD-006's finding (the corpus enumerates kernel members without ever stating a membership property) converges with the author's own two-K blocker (two definitions of K with no shared vocabulary) and 291 Audit A's graph-analysis finding of a missing mandatory-membership rule, but adds that 'kernel' may carry two distinct minimality criteria at once (engineering portability vs epistemic necessity), which would explain the two-vocabulary problem as an expected consequence rather than an anomaly -- recorded as an untested hypothesis, not a conclusion.

anchor: K_t -> Zero -> Determination -> Decision -> Authorization -> Action ... And it has five cuts, not three ... Wald has one cut where KnowledgeOS has four.
statement: The layered model's own operating pipeline is found to have five cuts (judging, choosing, authorizing, executing, plus the initial gap-detection) rather than the three-way Determination/Decision/Action split the author's theory-compatibility document had claimed as 'finer than Wald's two' -- an undercount corrected upward: Wald has one cut where KnowledgeOS's own pipeline has four.

anchor: "Probability IS knowledge itself" ... "One scalar probability defines knowledge" ... Negative convergence across independent traditions is the strongest evidence class available in this estate
statement: Three independent traditions (KnowledgeOS, Dretske information-flow theory, Kallenberg probability theory) all deny that probability alone constitutes or defines knowledge -- framed as negative convergence, argued to be the strongest available corroboration class for the corpus's own 2026-08-25 refutation of 'knowledge is conditional expectation,' and landing on the probability document's Kolmogorov-incompatible-and-declined verdict from two directions not used in that document.

anchor: Admissible(o,K) is the antecedent of every invariant in the I schema. It depends on Assurance, which the corpus has REFUTED as definable ... The invariant schema's antecedent cannot be decided.
statement: NG-1: Admissible(o,K), the antecedent of every invariant in the mandated invariant schema I, is undecidable because it depends on Assurance, a concept the corpus has refuted as definable, and the ratified admissibility condition is a 6-tuple with no admissibility conjunct of its own matching the dependent 7-tuple law -- classed BLOCKED-REQUIRES-DERIVATION and flagged as upstream of the author's own prior claim that I was the ultimate dependency root.

anchor: Gamma is derived and is not a component of K, so delta has nowhere to write a commitment. Executed result: K1 is K0 -- object identity, not merely equality. ... The central transition is a no-op in the only executable reading available.
statement: NG-2: because Gamma is derived rather than a stored component of K, the central state-transition operator delta has nowhere to commit a change; executed under the only available reading, delta produces K1 IS K0 (object identity, not merely equal values) -- called the deepest gap in the estate as it then stood, since invariants, congruence, the operation registry, Sigma's propagation and Zero's evaluation all presuppose delta changes something.

anchor: Phi : Pi_t -> K_t -- a SECOND undefined transformation ... Phi sits exactly where probability would become knowledge -- the step all three models jointly deny is automatic.
statement: NG-3: the layered pipeline X -> Y_t -> E_t -> F_t -> Pi_t -> K_t has two undefined arrows, not one -- the known Qualify:Y_t->E_t gap (G1) and a second, newly named Phi:Pi_t->K_t sitting exactly at the point where probability would become knowledge, which all three compared models jointly deny happens automatically; explicitly warned not to be merged with G1 since the two have different carriers and positions.

anchor: Pi -- provenance ... Policy ... probabilistic representation. ... A reader importing Pi as POLICY would silently re-read the programme's central normative question.
statement: NG-7: glyph collisions in the corpus's notation reached fifteen, two carrying normative stakes -- Pi is simultaneously used for provenance, for Policy, and for a probabilistic representation, such that a reader importing one sense for another would silently misread the programme's central normative question; classed as requiring a governance registry act (cheap, high-value, uncommissioned), distinct from NG-3's Phi collision (also independently discovered) between the second undefined transformation and the pre-existing Knowledge Qualification Problem's Phi.

anchor: three_model_convergence/: 1,279 files, 1,260 in the reading stage, 13 of 16 output lanes EMPTY ... the corpus has no mechanism that notices a commissioned step not being performed. ... That is the mechanism working, not failing.
statement: NG-9: the three_model_convergence protocol has processed only about 0.7% of its 2,321-file manifest (16 per-file records) with 13 of 16 output lanes empty, forbidding permanent classification during pass 1 by its own rule -- interpreted not as a failure but as an instance of a self-reporting mechanism (a progress.tsv) correctly working as designed, catching exactly the shape of gap a prior finding (PA-1) had predicted: the corpus otherwise has no mechanism that notices a commissioned step not being performed.

anchor: Three of the nine are upstream of my package's own foundations. That is the finding of this document.
statement: Summary placement of the nine new gaps: NG-1 (Admissible undecidable), NG-2 (delta has no commit case) and NG-4 (distinguishability not transitive) sit upstream of the invariant schema I, the operation set O, and every congruence claim including the author's own Sufficient(F,O,I); NG-3 and NG-5 are parallel/cheap decisions; NG-6, NG-8, NG-9 are hygiene issues, real but not blocking.

anchor: Zero is not an algebraic zero element. It is an algebraic/operational judgment of eliminability relative to a transformation and preservation contract.
statement: Renames the proposed 'Algebraic Zero' to Transformation-relative Zero, rejecting the term 'algebraic zero' as colliding with additive-identity/kernel meanings; freezes Zero_{T,Pi}(x) iff Pi(T(D))=Pi(T(D\x)) as the definition to preserve, over a general preservation contract Pi rather than the narrower (O_I,B_I) pair, motivated by cases such as governance-inquiry contracts Pi=(O,B,A_u) needing authorization constraints.

anchor: A direct sum requires substantial structure ... T_R(D) -> (Inv_T(D), Delta_R(D), Rem_T(D)) ... a structural decomposition, not yet an algebraic direct sum.
statement: Rejects the proposed algebraic claim T_R(D)=Inv_T(D)⊕Delta_R(D)⊕Rem_T(D) as too strong for a general corpus/graph/logical-theory/epistemic-state domain (a direct sum presupposes a common carrier, defined sum, independence, existence and uniqueness of decomposition), replacing it with a weaker structural mapping to a triple of observables, with the direct sum retained only as a possible special case in a particular mathematical regime.

anchor: But mathematically, projection normally has an idempotence property ... elimination can change the context for subsequent eliminations.
statement: Warns against calling the elimination/retention operator L_{T,I} a 'projection operator' before idempotence L(L(D))=L(D) is established, illustrating with a three-element example (removing a makes b redundant, then removing b makes c redundant) where one-pass and iterative elimination differ; proposes testing three possible outcomes for L^2 vs L: idempotent, order-dependent (L_a L_b != L_b L_a), or a fixed-point/normalization process D_{n+1}=L(D_n).

anchor: Eliminate(x) != Delete(x). Deletion is an operation on data. Elimination is a justified epistemic decision.
statement: Introduces the Zero Witness W_x=(Observation,Transformation,PreservationComparison,DecisionBasis) as a first-class object answering what was observed, what transformation applied, what preservation claim was tested, and what evidence justified the Zero decision, establishing that Zero(x) implies EliminationCandidate(x) but not necessarily Delete(x) -- the system may retain the original material and record only the Zero status plus witness.

anchor: Can M be selected without presupposing the desired result? ... M must be independently declared or mechanically derivable.
statement: Splits Method Selection M(D,I,C,R)->T into three kinds -- human-declared M_human, rule-based M_rule, and learned M_theta -- explicitly deferring the learned kind because a model could otherwise learn to 'choose whatever transformation makes the desired information disappear,' which would destroy the validity of the Zero experiment; for initial experiments M must be independently declared or mechanically derivable.

anchor: R_0=symbols/positions ... R_5=epistemic interpretation ... What previously invisible distinction became preservable?
statement: Defines an observability ladder of representations R_0 (symbols/positions) through R_5 (epistemic interpretation), and introduces 'representation-induced Zero': if a coarser representation R_1 cannot distinguish two states that a richer R_2 can, then Zero_{R_1}(x) may hold while Zero_{R_2}(x) does not, giving a falsification mechanism (increase representational resolution and test whether prior Zero judgments survive) for representation-dependent information loss.

anchor: Experiment discovers required operations ... Corpus -> Representation -> Observable distinctions -> Required operations -> Algebra.
statement: States the governing methodological principle for the whole research programme: do not choose the algebra first and force the epistemic problem into it; instead let experiments discover which operations (Combine, Compare, Differentiate, Transform, Eliminate, Retain, Reconstruct) are actually required, and only then ask whether they admit an algebraic structure. Freezes the Vedic-material epistemic-status table (transformation strategies=[EXT], candidate transformations=[PROP], improved extraction=[EXP], representation-independence/minimal-carrier/carrier-correspondence-to-Select=[OPEN]) and the negative statement Vedic Mathematics != KnowledgeOS Algebra.

anchor: Do not compare number bases. Compare representation algebras. ... R*=argmin_{R in R} Complexity(R) subject to Adequacy(R,D,Pi,I,C,R_reasoning)>=tau
statement: Sharpens the planned EXP-1 (comparing R_2,R_3,R_5,R_8,R_10,R_20,R_30) into two separate axes -- encoding basis B (how values are written, probably secondary) versus semantic carrier V (which carrier preserves the distinctions Pi requires) -- warning that a 30-valued representation could have HIGHER loss than a smaller structured representation, i.e. 'representation adequacy is not monotonic in the number of available values'; and revises the closing master formulation from R*=argmin Complexity(R) s.t. Loss(R,Pi)=0 to the softer R*=argmin Complexity(R) s.t. Adequacy(R,D,Pi,I,C,R_reasoning)>=tau, since demanding exactly zero loss may be impossible for real text while a representation losing only Pi-irrelevant distinctions is still fully useful. Adds EXP-0 Representation Independence: test Zero_{R1,Pi}(x) <=> Zero_{R2,Pi}(x) under a declared mapping f:R1->R2, with three possible outcomes (stable, representation-induced, incomparable), connecting to the frozen FR-001 result that representation and distinguishability must not be conflated with equivalence.

anchor: The one derivation it ever prompted -- the Zero/Sunya chain -- was earned by 1,620,000 assignments, not by the reading.
statement: Reports that the KR-ZERO-ALGEBRA-2026-09 experiment executed 1,620,000 assignments in generating its test corpus, and that the Gita text's role was confined to producing questions and lenses, with the actual Zero/Sunya chain result earned entirely by that computation, not by the philosophical reading.

anchor: no embodied being can relinquish actions without remainder ... A total-elimination operator is not merely hard to build; the target state may not exist.
statement: Lens L-1: Gita 18.11/3.5's claim that no embodied being can act without remainder is read as a lens (not evidence) suggesting a total-elimination operator's target state may not exist at all, noted as merely consistent with (not established by) the experiment's own measured termination (H3, <=2 iterations) and monotonicity (H4) results.

anchor: Five of nine findings get nothing from the text -- including every one of the algebraic results.
statement: Explicit corroboration-map audit: of nine KR-ZERO-ALGEBRA findings tested against the Gita text, five get nothing (H5/H6 non-element-wise results, non-confluence/order-dependence, termination in <=2 iterations, and H9 invariant-orthogonal-to-Zero all have no textual counterpart), arguing this is the expected shape since 'the text speaks to the ethics of elimination, not to its algebra.'

anchor: The kernel remains NOT SELECTABLE. Nothing in this study bears on it. ... it is now the fourth consecutive time this strand has produced none.
statement: Refuses to name any kernel candidate from the Gita reading, citing the experiment's own final-status rule (do not declare Zero a kernel primitive, do not declare the Vedic analogy canonical), the C-1 usability-does-not-imply-kernel-membership rule, and the layer ban on Gita-concept-to-primitive derivation, noting this is the fourth consecutive Gita-corroboration study to yield zero kernel entities.

anchor: Object = Reference + Deviation ... The base does not have to be numeric ... Base = Reference Model
statement: Abstracts the Vedic 'base and deviation' multiplication method (e.g. computing 95x92 via deviations from 100) into Object=Reference+Deviation and a typed Represent(D|K0)=(K0,Delta_{K0}(D),R_{K0}(D)), generalizing the base K0 beyond numeric to textual/ontological/temporal/inquiry-relative/organizational reference models, e.g. a reference architecture document as K0 against which a new document's deviation is computed.

anchor: Vertically and Crosswise ... Interaction = Direct Relations + Cross Relations ... an information relation algebra.
statement: Abstracts the Vedic 'vertically and crosswise' multiplication procedure (computing (a+b)(c+d) as ac+ad+bc+bd) into a candidate Cross(X,Y) relational-interaction operation over the dimensions of two information objects, illustrated with a worked example (Document A's Authentication/Tenant/User dimensions crossed with Document B's Keycloak/Realm/Role dimensions) revealing relevant crosswise relations (Tenant<->Realm, User<->Role, Authentication<->Keycloak) among mostly-irrelevant combinations.

anchor: Alternative Elimination and Retention ... D -> (E,R) ... E = {x in D : Zero_{T,Pi}(x)}.
statement: Identifies the Vedic sutra 'By Alternative Elimination and Retention' as almost directly usable: abstracted as D->(E,R) with E the eliminated candidates under the declared method and R the retained remainder, directly combined with the KR-ZERO-ALGEBRA Zero definition as E={x in D: Zero_{T,Pi}(x)}, with every elimination assigned a witness x->W_x.

anchor: K = (B, Delta, I, R, Gamma) ... Observe, Base, Diff, Cross, Transform, Eliminate, Retain, Verify, Compose
statement: Proposes a Candidate Transformation Algebra with carrier K=(B,Delta,I,R,Gamma) (base/reference, differences, invariants, remainder, boundary/context constraints) and nine candidate operations (Observe, Base, Diff, Cross, Transform, Eliminate, Retain, Verify, Compose), explicitly deferring the question of whether these satisfy identity, composition, associativity, idempotence, commutativity, conservation, remainder stability, or Zero compositionality to future experiments rather than assuming any of them.

anchor: Can the structural principles underlying multiple Vedic transformations be abstracted into a general algebra of information transformation? ... take one very small corpus and implement perhaps only five operations: Base, Diff, Cross, Eliminate, Remainder.
statement: Proposes reframing the research question from 'can Vedic Mathematics solve text?' to whether structural principles across multiple Vedic sutras generalize into an information-transformation algebra, and proposes a minimal new research lane implementing five base operations (Base, Diff, Cross, Eliminate, Remainder) on a small corpus before asking what algebraic structure their composition forms.

anchor: Zero_{T,Pi}(x) is not an element property. It is a property of an element in a representation, context, transformation, inquiry, and preservation contract.
statement: Headline interpretation of the executed KR-ZERO-ALGEBRA-2026-09 results: nine of eleven algebraic hypotheses (L^2=L; L_A L_B=L_B L_A; individual-implies-group Zero H5; group-implies-individual Zero H6; reference-independence H7; contract-independence H8; invariant=Zero H9; Remainder=simple-set-subtraction H10; heuristic=counterfactual H11) were refuted, while termination (H3) and monotone decrease (H4) held (tested with 1,200 cases per family, deterministic execution), interpreted not as a failed theory but as evidence the counterfactual definition of Zero is correct while the assumption that x is the fundamental carrier is wrong.

anchor: D=[x,x] ... individual: {x}->Zero, {x}->Zero; group: {x1,x2}->NOT Zero ... D=[+c,-c] ... group: {+c,-c}->Zero
statement: Reports the two generated minimal witnesses refuting element-wise Zero in both directions: a duplicate/redundancy case D=[x,x] where each x is individually Zero but the pair jointly is not (Zero(x,D) & Zero(y,D) does not imply Zero({x,y},D)); and a cancellation case D=[+c,-c] where neither element is individually Zero but the pair is jointly eliminable (the converse failure), together establishing that Zero is potentially a property of a subset S subseteq D rather than an element predicate.

anchor: The heuristic and counterfactual paths agree only 55.75%. ... 1559 elements were removed by the heuristic despite not satisfying the counterfactual criterion, whereas only 301 true Zero elements were retained.
statement: Reports the PATH-A (formal counterfactual) vs PATH-B (declared heuristic rule) agreement rate of 55.75%, with a strongly asymmetric error pattern -- 1,559 over-removed by the heuristic against only 301 true-Zero elements the heuristic failed to remove -- establishing an empirical over-elimination bias and the concrete distinction HeuristicElimination != CounterfactualZero.

anchor: terminating but non-confluent rewriting ... We didn't choose rewriting theory. The experiment is telling us that rewriting theory may be the appropriate mathematical regime.
statement: Interprets the combined termination+non-confluence result as evidence the elimination process is better modelled as a terminating, non-confluent rewriting system (where different orderings L_A L_B(D) != L_B L_A(D) reach different normal forms) than as a classical commutative algebra or idempotent projection, framed as an instance of discovering the required mathematical structure from behaviour rather than choosing it in advance.

anchor: KR-ZERO-GROUP-2026-09 ... What is the minimal mathematical structure of group-level eliminability?
statement: Proposes a follow-on experiment KR-ZERO-GROUP-2026-09 to test Zero(S;D) for subsets S subseteq D directly, investigating singleton-vs-group Zero, pairwise-vs-higher-order Zero, cancellation, redundancy, order-dependence, minimal/maximal eliminable subsets, overlapping Zero subsets, and whether the resulting family structure is better described by rewriting systems, hypergraphs, closure systems, or lattices -- deferring any algebra question until after this experiment.

anchor: The experiment directly tested the definition on 4,203 element cases and found that the heuristic and counterfactual notions agree only 55.75% ... The report explicitly records 131 and 63 witnesses respectively.
statement: Precise figures for the KR-ZERO-ALGEBRA executed results: 4,203 element-level test cases; 131 redundancy witnesses (D=[x,x] shape) and 63 cancellation witnesses (D=[+c,-c] shape), both falsifying element-wise Zero in opposite directions; the process is terminating and monotone but non-confluent, with simultaneous/forward-sequential/reverse-sequential processing diverging in 169 of 1,189 cases, traced concretely to removing token 'ref1' causing two 'c' tokens to become adjacent and activate a context-dependent transformation rule.

anchor: 1,223 cases where the visible result remained unchanged after removal, but 196 of those were rejected once the full boundary contract was considered. That's 16.03%.
statement: Precise boundary-preservation result: of 1,223 cases where removing a candidate left the visible answer unchanged, 196 (16.03%) were rejected once provenance/uncertainty/scope/contradiction were added to the preservation contract, taken as direct experimental confirmation that 'same visible result does not imply same epistemic state.'

anchor: A = D - Eliminated and contract-unresolved material C agree exactly in all 1,182 tested cases. But transformation residual B differs.
statement: H10 result: of three candidate Remainder constructions (A = D minus eliminated elements; B = transformation residual; C = contract-relevant unresolved material), A and C coincide exactly across all 1,182 tested cases while B differs, establishing that the original three-way Invariant⊕Difference⊕Remainder decomposition is inappropriate and that Remainder is better understood as multiple empirically distinct observables produced by different questions rather than a single algebraic component.

anchor: Is the missing mathematics a richer number system, or a richer carrier? ... the failures are increasingly about structure, not cardinality.
statement: Argues the experiment's failures ([x,x] requiring contextual multiplicity, [+c,-c] requiring interaction/cancellation, the boundary result requiring a tuple (Value,Boundary,Provenance,...)) are about representational STRUCTURE rather than the number of available values, so a 30-valued scalar algebra could still fail where a small relational structure succeeds -- reframing the original 'which number base' question as 'is the missing mathematics a richer number system or a richer carrier', to be tested empirically rather than assumed either way.

anchor: Suppose P(C)=0.9 and P(O(T(D))=Q(D)|C)=1. The representation could be completely wrong when C is false. ... conditional zero loss => all representations satisfy constraints is invalid.
statement: Identifies an invalid step in a submitted proof: a definition of zero loss conditioned on a valid region (P(O(T(D))=Q(D) | AND_i c_i(T(D))=1)=1) does not imply the necessity claim that the representation's support lies entirely within that valid region, since the representation could be arbitrarily wrong when the condition is false; repairs it by defining zero loss as two separate unconditional requirements (P(C(T(D)))=1 and P(O(T(D))=Q(D))=1) or by restricting the theorem to an explicit valid domain X_Pi={D: for all i, c_i(T(D))=1}.

anchor: Probabilistic zero loss: Q(D)=O(T(D)) P-a.s. ... Structural / pointwise zero loss: T(D1)=T(D2) => Q(D1)=Q(D2) for all D1,D2.
statement: Distinguishes two versions of a fiber-preservation condition that a submitted proof had conflated: probabilistic zero loss (Q(D)=O(T(D)) almost surely) versus structural/pointwise zero loss (deterministic fiber preservation for all D1,D2, not merely almost-surely); shows for deterministic Q that I(D;Q(D)|T(D))=0 is equivalent to H(Q(D)|T(D))=0, so the submitted proof's two stated conditions are not independent unless a pointwise (not merely a.s.) theorem is specifically wanted.

anchor: kernel normally belongs to a structure where such a notion is defined ... For now I would use Null_Pi(T) = {S: Pi(T(D))=Pi(T(D\S))} or ZeroSet_{T,Pi}(D) = {S subseteq D: Zero_{T,Pi}(S;D)}.
statement: Judges a submitted 'kernel' notation S in ker(T_Pi) premature since no ambient algebraic structure (homomorphism, distinguished zero element) has yet been established for the representation-reduction setting, proposing Null_Pi(T) / ZeroSet_{T,Pi}(D) as neutral placeholders pending discovery of whether kernel-like properties actually hold -- preserving the discipline of not assuming algebraic structure before observing it.

anchor: H(R*) >= H(Q(D)) + H(C(D)|Q(D)) ... If the contract requires c_i(R)=1 with probability 1, then C_R=(1,...,1) is constant and H(C_R)=0. So the bound becomes simply H(R*) >= H(Q(D)).
statement: Corrects a submitted entropy lower bound: the constraint term should be the vector of realized predicate outcomes C_R=(c_1(R),...,c_k(R)) rather than the abstract predicate set C(D), and since a contract requiring c_i(R)=1 with probability 1 makes C_R a constant (H(C_R)=0), the bound collapses to the clean H(R*)>=H(Q(D)); also recommends separating Shannon entropy (for probabilistic experiments) from Kolmogorov complexity (for structural representations) as two distinct later research tracks rather than mixing them in one definition.

anchor: So 5 digits -> 2 digits is indeed the right intuition -- but the mathematical object we are searching for is not digit reduction. It is contract-relative representation reduction.
statement: Reframes the '5 digits->2 digits' intuition rigorously: the question is not digit count but whether Q(D)=O(R2), i.e. whether the reduced representation R2 is zero-loss RELATIVE to (Q,Pi); if adequate and no smaller representation works, R2=R*_Pi is a candidate minimal adequate representation -- proposing 'can Vedic transformations discover minimal adequate representations?' as the sharpened research question, and renaming the target object 'Entropy-Minimal Adequate Representation' to distinguish it from other minimality notions (description/dimension/cardinality/structural/computational).

anchor: How much representation can be eliminated while remaining in the same inquiry-relevant equivalence class and satisfying the preservation contract? ... This is NOT fundamentally a question about digit count.
statement: States the central research question of the new phase in general form (not the '5-digit to 2-digit' motivating example): given source representation D, inquiry Q, constraints C, decoder O, and transformation family T, how far can representation be reduced before preservation fails; formalizes the preservation contract as Pi=(Q,C,O) and the admissible domain X_{Pi,T}={D: C(T(D))=1}.

anchor: H_hat(Q|R)=0 means no observed R-fiber contains conflicting Q values. This is evidence about the observed population, not proof of generalization to an unseen population.
statement: States Theorem 1 (adequacy H(Q(D)|T(D))=0 iff an optimal decoder O* exists with P(O*(T(D))=Q(D))=1) and mandates that empirical adequacy (H_hat, measured on a finite dataset) must never be silently promoted to theoretical/population adequacy (H); defines the structural audit N_viol(R)=#{(Da,Db): R(Da)=R(Db) and Q(Da)!=Q(Db)}, shown equivalent to H_hat(Q|R)=0 under the standard empirical distribution, to be reported alongside the entropy summary.

anchor: H(T) = H(Q) + H(T|Q) ... Do NOT call this objectively superfluous information. Correct terminology: inquiry-extraneous representation relative to Q.
statement: States Theorem 2 (Q factors through T on the admissible domain, Q-factorized/Q-equivalent, explicitly not automatically a bijection) and Theorem 3 (an information lower bound H(T*)>=H(Q) for T* minimizing entropy among adequate transformations, with equality iff H(T|Q)=0), deriving the central decomposition H(T)=H(Q)+H(T|Q) and insisting the excess term H(T|Q) be called 'inquiry-extraneous representation relative to Q,' never 'objectively superfluous,' since extraneousness is contract-relative.

anchor: Elim_{T,Pi}(D) = {S: D in X_{Pi,T} and E_S(D) in X_{Pi,T} and O(T(D))=O(T(E_S(D)))=Q(D)} ... Zero(a1;D) AND Zero(a2;D) does NOT imply Zero({a1,a2};D).
statement: Defines the Contractually Eliminable Set Elim_{T,Pi}(D) without assuming the naive E_S(D)=D\S elimination operator, and generalizes Zero to a subset-relative, non-element-wise predicate Zero_{T,Pi}(S;D) iff Pi(T(D))=Pi(T(E_S(D))), citing the deduplication witness D=[a,a,b,b] where individual occurrences are eliminable but eliminating both occurrences of a simultaneously changes the representation -- concluding eliminability may be relational and Zero must remain defined over subsets/groups where appropriate.

Reports the published aggregate of the higher-order-Zero experiment KR-ZERO-ORDER-2026-09: of 1,395 cases, 89.7% resolve at interaction order k=1, 1.8% at k=2, 0.2% at k=3, and 8.24% are irreducible; per-transformation interaction rates vary sharply (T2 dedup 31.46%, T8 interacting 20.59%, T4 context 11.50%, T1/T5/T7 0%, T3/T6 <1%); and monotonicity of interaction order in subset size holds in 387 of 391 tested cases but is explicitly NOT a universal law, so the conclusion 'Zero is fundamentally higher-order' must not be drawn from a non-negligible but minority irreducible class.

anchor: R1, R2, R3, R4 ... are REPRESENTATION CLASSES. They are NOT R5 -> R4 -> R3 -> R2 -> R1 reduction levels. There is a dangerous naming collision.
statement: Issues a critical, explicitly labelled warning against a naming collision: the old KR-ZERO experiment's R1-R4 labels denote representation CLASSES (token sequence, token sequence+metadata, graph/relational, structured claim/evidence), independently sampled with no R_n->R_{n-1} transformation between them, and must never be reinterpreted as levels of the new sequential R5->R4->R3->R2->R1 reduction hierarchy; a grep/audit found zero evidence in the old KR-ZERO corpus for Q(D), R5, C(Rn), O(Rn), representation_hierarchy, or reduction_level, so KR-ZERO-ORDER != KR-REP-DATASET.

anchor: RULE 1: Inspect before hypothesizing. ... RULE 10: Persist the full experimental population.
statement: States a ten-rule research discipline for the new KR-REP-REDUCTION-2026-09 experiment (inspect before hypothesizing; never infer a hierarchy from naming alone; never fabricate missing case-level data; separate old experiments from new theoretical constructs; separate empirical results from mathematical claims; separate adequacy from realization; separate entropy from representation size/capacity; never assume algebraic structure before proving/observing it; preserve negative results and falsifications; persist the full experimental population, never only failures/witnesses/aggregates), and specifies a six-phase Claude Code audit protocol (A Inventory, B Classify Artifacts, C Verify Old KR-ZERO, D Protect Against R1-R4 Collision, E Theory-to-Corpus Gap matrix with status vocabulary IMPLEMENTED/PARTIAL/EMPIRICALLY TESTED/THEORETICAL ONLY/ABSENT/CONFLICTING, F New Experiment Design) that must produce a first-response inventory-classify-verify-map-design report BEFORE any implementation, explicitly rejecting an ASSUME->ADAPT->FABRICATE sequence.

anchor: corpus/cases.jsonl -- primary file ... 1,395 level-test records ... corpus/subsets.jsonl -- 14,194 individual subset-level records.
statement: Specifies the priority-ordered artifact list for auditing the old KR-ZERO corpus: cases.jsonl (1,395 level-test records, the correct unit for validating the published aggregates), subsets.jsonl (14,194 individual subset-level records, needed to inspect actual S-level Zero behaviour and higher-order elimination witnesses), property-results.json (the ~4.7KB published ground-truth aggregate: 1,395 cases, k=1:1252, k=2:25, k=3:3, irreducible:115), emit_corpus.py (the deterministic seeded generator proving the corpus is not a hand-produced reconstruction), and CORPUS-AUDIT.md (prior audit context) -- explicitly excluding the 481 irreducible-witness tail sample as a primary dataset and warning against constructing a KR-REP-DATASET from the old R1-R4 labels, which would be a category error.

anchor: aggregate KR-ZERO results != case-level KR-REP dataset ... If the underlying cases were never persisted -- only the aggregate results were saved -- then we cannot reconstruct the 1,395 cases without fabrication.
statement: Establishes that the visible material discusses KR-ZERO's results and structure but does not itself contain the actual 1,395-record case-level dataset, and warns that if only aggregate results were ever persisted (not the underlying cases), reconstruction would require fabrication -- an important possible audit finding in its own right, distinct from and prior to any KR-REP-DATASET construction.

anchor: N_n={i: R_{n,i} != NULL} and Comp_n=|N_n|/|N| ... we should never silently normalize those differences away.
statement: Corrects a denominator conflict in the dataset-construction protocol: per-level metrics (A_n, F_n, H_hat(Q|R_n), H_hat(R_n|Q)) must be computed over the level-specific usable support N_n={i: R_{n,i}!=NULL}, with completeness Comp_n=|N_n|/|N| reported separately from the fixed source corpus size |N|=1395, given the historical KR-ZERO denominators already disagree (1395, 1496, 1475) and must never be silently reconciled away; recommends requiring Comp_n=1 for any level used to establish the primary boundary n*, with partial-support results explicitly labelled as such.

anchor: D_REP = {(D_i,Q_i,R_{5,i},R_{4,i},R_{3,i},R_{2,i},R_{1,i}, C_{1..5},O_{1..5})} ... No empirical result is promoted to a population-level theorem.
statement: Freezes the KR-REP-DATASET dataset contract D_REP with seven governing rules: no synthetic intermediate states; Q_i established independently from R_n; every missing representation explicitly NULL/UNOBSERVED; every metric reports its actual denominator N_n; completeness reported separately; KR-ZERO's original classifications remain provenance fields, not newly inferred labels; no empirical result promoted to a population-level theorem.

anchor: those results do not yet provide, for every source sample, R5,R4,R3,R2,R1 with a common Q, O, and C at each representation level. So using the KR-ZERO results directly would mix two experimental protocols.
statement: Establishes that the existing KR-ZERO empirical cases (D,S,T,Pi,Q,Zero-status; order results k=1..3/irreducible; the dedup witness D=[a,a,b,b]) do not supply, for every sample, a common R5..R1 chain with shared Q/O/C at each level, so using them directly for the new representation-reduction calculation would improperly mix two distinct experimental protocols; recommends the minimum canonical schema table (Sample, D, Q, R5..R1) plus per-level (C(Rn), O(Rn)) and warns that Q must never be generated from R_n, on pain of manufacturing H(Q|R_n)=0 artificially.

anchor: V_r = [(sum_q c_{r,q})^2 - sum_q c_{r,q}^2] / 2 and N_viol = sum_r V_r.
statement: Derives a closed-form, efficient formula for the fiber-violation count: for an R-fiber with per-Q-value counts c_{r,q1}..c_{r,qk}, the number of conflicting unordered pairs is V_r=[(sum_q c_{r,q})^2 - sum_q c_{r,q}^2]/2, and N_viol=sum_r V_r, avoiding repeated list-count operations and clarifying the statistic's combinatorial meaning; also recommends explicit canonicalized-equality semantics for R_n and Q comparisons rather than implicit Python object equality, since the KR-ZERO corpus may contain structured objects.

anchor: do not assume that the existing k=1, k=2, k=3, irreducible labels correspond directly to R1,...,R5. They are classifications of elimination behavior, whereas Rn are representation states. That mapping must be demonstrated from the corpus.
statement: Adds a transformation-registry schema (transformation_id, input_level, output_level, transformation_definition, source_provenance, reconstruction_status) so that any measured information loss between representation levels can be attributed to a specific operation, and restates the R1-R4-vs-reduction-hierarchy warning in dataset-construction terms: the next operation must be to inspect the actual KR-ZERO corpus schema empirically, never to write a mapping parser from specification alone.

anchor: Do not create synthetic data. Do not infer missing representation states. Do not silently reconcile denominators. Do not reinterpret historical k classifications as representation levels.
statement: States the four governing prohibitions for the KR-REP-DATASET-2026-09 production audit, and specifies Phase 2's denominator-reconciliation table (KR-ZERO baseline, O2, O4, O6 populations) that must explain 1395, 1496 and 1475 as either different populations, different filtering stages, duplicated cases, or reporting inconsistencies, explicitly without repairing the historical numbers.

anchor: Q explicitly evaluated from raw D or Q deterministically reproducible from raw D. Reject: Q derived from R_n, Q inferred from Zero-status, Q reconstructed from the desired experimental outcome.
statement: Specifies Phase 4's independent-Q audit, accepting only an inquiry answer Q(D_i) that is explicitly evaluated from or deterministically reproducible from the raw source D, rejecting any Q derived from a reduced representation, from Zero-status, or from the desired outcome, with unverifiable independence recorded as Q=NULL / Q_independence_status=UNVERIFIED rather than manufacturing ground truth.

anchor: n* = min{n: Comp_n=1 and A_n=1 and N_viol_n=0 and H_hat(Q|R_n)<=epsilon}. If no level satisfies this: n*=NULL, and that is a valid scientific result. Do not lower the completeness requirement to manufacture an n*.
statement: Specifies Phase 10's canonical minimal-adequate-level definition n*, requiring full completeness (Comp_n=1) before a level may establish the boundary, explicitly stating that n*=NULL is a valid scientific outcome and that the completeness requirement must never be lowered merely to manufacture a positive n*; Phase 11 then separates three independently reportable boundary-diagnosis dimensions (Representation: N_viol>0 or H(Q|R)>0; Contract: A(R)<1; Operator: H(Q|R)=0 and F(R)<1), explicitly non-mutually-exclusive.

anchor: N_viol(R)=0 <=> H_hat(Q|R)=0, not merely N_viol=0 => H_hat(Q|R)=0 ... The asymmetry is diagnostic rather than logical.
statement: Strengthens a stated implication into a full equivalence: for finite empirical support, N_viol(R)=0 and H_hat(Q|R)=0 are logically equivalent adequacy conditions (since zero conditional entropy forces every observed R-fiber to a single Q-value and vice versa), but the two remain diagnostically distinct -- N_viol as a structural witness locating collisions, H_hat(Q|R) as an information summary of remaining uncertainty.

anchor: R_{n*} is adequate, R_{n*-1} is inadequate, B_{n*}: R_{n*} -> R_{n*-1}. If adequacy is non-monotone across the chain, record that as an experimental finding rather than assuming a single boundary.
statement: Requires the boundary transition B_{n*} to be defined only when both the adjacency condition (R_{n*} adequate) and its failure (R_{n*-1} inadequate) are established, distinguishing 'lowest adequate level,' 'first preservation failure,' and 'boundary transition' as three concepts that coincide only under monotone preservation behaviour across the reduction chain.

anchor: H(R|Q)>0 => R contains variation not determined by Q ... This variation is Q-extraneous relative to the inquiry, but is not necessarily useless information.
statement: Refines the interpretation of H(R|Q)>0 from 'R contains non-inquiry payload' to the more precise 'R contains variation not determined by Q,' explicitly noting this Q-extraneous variation may still be valuable for provenance, auditability, explainability, or answering a different future inquiry -- so H(R|Q)=0 means 'no Q-extraneous variation,' not 'nothing else is useful.'

anchor: A: Is R sufficient? <-> N_viol, H_hat(Q|R). B: Does O realize the contract? <-> A(R), F(R). C: How much Q-extraneous representation remains? <-> H_hat(R|Q). D: Where does reduction cross the boundary? <-> n*.
statement: Freezes a four-question decomposition of the KR-REP-REDUCTION protocol (sufficiency, contract realization, excess representation, boundary) each matched to a specific empirical observable (N_viol/H_hat(Q|R); A(R)/F(R); H_hat(R|Q); n*), and separates three independently-diagnosable boundary-failure kinds (Representation Boundary: N_viol>0 or H(Q|R)>0; Contract Boundary: A(R)<1; Operator Boundary: H(Q|R)=0 but F(R)<1), noting 'information was lost != contract was violated != decoder was inadequate' as three genuinely different failure modes that a reduction can exhibit.

anchor: The audit's findings -- 1,395 verified, 0/33,840, 40.2% class contamination -- are exactly as strong before and after this document.
statement: Reports three concrete figures from the executed KR-REP-REDUCTION corpus audit as of 2026-09-03: 1,395 verified cases, a 0/33,840 result (a zero-count structural check over 33,840 items, consistent in scale with the subsets.jsonl-derived pairwise counts discussed elsewhere in the thread), and a 40.2% class-contamination finding -- all stated to be unaffected in strength by the philosophical corroboration study itself.

anchor: This is the 5 digits -> 2 digits trap in Sanskrit dress. ... A reading that treats compactness as a virtue would import exactly the error the mandate forbids.
statement: Explicitly refuses the most tempting available reading -- that Gita 2.50 ('yoga is skill in action') licenses treating representational compactness as inherently virtuous -- citing the master handoff's section 25 warning that digit count is not itself a representation-capacity measure and that a two-digit representation may carry MORE information capacity than a five-digit one depending on encoding, recording the refusal as the study's most useful yield.

anchor: A two-state representation can have entropy close to 1 bit, while a larger representation can have much lower entropy if its distribution is highly concentrated. ... distinguish representation capacity, storage cost, Shannon entropy, minimality.
statement: Rejects a proposed requirement of strictly decreasing entropy H(R_n)<H(R_{n+1}) across the reduction chain as too strong, since entropy depends on the induced probability distribution rather than representation size; recommends requiring strictly decreasing representation CAPACITY instead, and measuring entropy, storage cost, and minimality as independent, separately reported quantities.

anchor: A failed representation transition Rn -> Rn-1 demonstrates that the transformation does not preserve the contract for that sample. It does not automatically identify a unique payload S that was removed.
statement: Warns against over-interpreting a failed reduction step: multiple eliminated components, interaction effects, transformation-induced changes, recombination, or loss of relational structure could all produce the same observed failure, so a specific eliminated set S notin Elim_{T,Pi}(D) may only be inferred when T_n has an explicit, declared elimination decomposition T_n=E_{S_n} -- otherwise report only 'T_n crosses the preservation boundary for D_i,' connecting this directly to the KR-ZERO-ORDER finding that transformation loss should not be assumed to decompose element-wise.

anchor: H(T)=H(Q)+H(T|Q), therefore H(T)>=H(Q), with equality iff H(T|Q)=0 ... T(D) = G(Q(D)) almost surely ... T(D) and Q(D) are mutually deterministically recoverable almost surely.
statement: Confirms Theorem 3's corrected attainability condition H(T(D)|Q(D))=0 and its consequence H(T)=H(Q)+H(T|Q); corrects the proposed 'Level 4: Q-Isomorphic Representation' (from Q=O∘T alone) to 'Q-Equivalent Representation,' since factorization through T establishes only that T contains enough information to determine Q, not a bijection between the full codomains Y and Q-space; the stronger, correct claim requires both H(Q(D)|T(D))=0 and H(T(D)|Q(D))=0, giving mutual a.s. recoverability T(D) <-> Q(D) rather than an unproven isomorphism.

anchor: sim_{Pi,T} = sim_Q restricted to X_{Pi,T} ... T(D) cannot literally be an element of [D]_{sim_Pi} ... D sim_{Pi,T} E_S(D) because Q(D)=Q(E_S(D)).
statement: Repairs two structural errors: (1) the equivalence relation sim_Pi must be defined as the global Q-induced relation sim_Q restricted to the T-dependent admissible domain X_{Pi,T}, not as an independent relation whose domain and defining condition are conflated; (2) a 'same fiber' claim mixing source-space [D]_{sim_Pi} (subset of X) with representation-space elements T(D), T(E_S(D)) (elements of Y) is type-incorrect -- the correct statement is D sim_{Pi,T} E_S(D) in source space, with O(T(D))=O(T(E_S(D))) as the separate representation-space consequence.

anchor: T_Adeq(Q) = {T: H(Q(D)|T(D))=0} ... T_Real(Pi) = {T: P(D in X_{Pi,T})=1 and P(O(T(D))=Q(D))=1}.
statement: Separates a previously ambiguous family T_adequate(Pi) into two explicitly distinct families -- T_Adeq(Q) (transformations adequate for the inquiry alone) and T_Real(Pi) (transformations that additionally realize the whole contract, both admissibility and the fixed decoder) -- and cautions that entropy minimization T*=argmin H(T(D)) should be stated as an infimum unless existence of the minimizer is separately established.

anchor: ord_{T,Pi}(S;D) = min{k: Zero(S;D) is decidable from admissible information of order <= k}.
statement: Defines a provisional (explicitly research, not ratified) interaction-order function ord_{T,Pi}(S;D) as the minimal information order at which Zero(S;D) becomes decidable, proposing to test whether order 1/2/3 correspond respectively to independent/local eliminability, pairwise interaction, and genuine three-way interaction, or whether that interpretation is false.

anchor: N_generated = N_eligible + N_excluded + N_vacuous + N_invalid + ... 1500 != 1395 != 1496 != 1475 cannot simply be left implicit.
statement: Demands a case-accounting identity reconciling every observed KR-ZERO population denominator (1500, 1395, 1496, 1475) before treating any percentage (89.7%, 8.24%, 90.04%, 7.89%) as a headline empirical estimate, framing this as an experimental-validity issue rather than documentation housekeeping.

anchor: ORDER -> MECHANISM -> CARRIER -> REPRESENTATION REDUCTION ... KR-ZERO-MECHANISM-2026-09 ... let the mechanism experiment constrain the choice.
statement: Recommends resequencing the research programme as ORDER -> MECHANISM -> CARRIER -> REPRESENTATION REDUCTION (rather than jumping straight to representation reduction), proposing a new experiment KR-ZERO-MECHANISM-2026-09 with three gates (denominator reconciliation; complete witness extraction for the 115 irreducible cases with a per-witness mechanism/minimal-dependency table; mechanism classification), so the eventual mathematical carrier (multiset, graph, hypergraph, rewrite system) is discovered from the elimination mechanism rather than promoted in advance.

anchor: the old generator itself is defective. R1 was supposed to mean token-only, but 103/256 R1 contexts contain metadata because three generator shapes bypass the class constructor.
statement: Reports the CORPUS-THEORY-AUDIT.md finding that the old KR-ZERO representation-class generator is itself defective: 103 of 256 contexts labelled R1 (intended to mean token-only) actually contain metadata, because three code paths in the generator bypass its own class constructor -- meaning the old representation-class experiment cannot be used to support any claim about representation reduction, independent of the R1-R4-vs-hierarchy naming-collision issue.

anchor: The critical finding is that the new chain does not currently exist in the repository. The audit explicitly finds the chain, inquiry Q, constraints C, decoder O, adequacy, fiber analysis, H(R|Q), metric vector, and held-out evaluation absent.
statement: Confirms the CORPUS-THEORY-AUDIT.md's finding that none of the elements the new representation-reduction theory requires (the R5->R2 chain itself, an independently-defined Q, C, O, fiber analysis, H(R|Q), the metric vector, held-out evaluation) exist anywhere in the repository yet, so the next task must be experiment DESIGN, never immediate dataset construction or implementation.

anchor: Do NOT assume that E_S(D)=D\S is valid ... Define Q : X -> Answers BEFORE defining transformations T5...T2 ... At the end provide a concise verdict: READY FOR IMPLEMENTATION or NOT READY.
statement: Specifies the sixteen-section design-only prompt for KR-REP-REDUCTION-DESIGN-2026-09.md (carrier; source representation D; inquiry Q defined independently and prior to the transformations; contract C; a fixed decoder O separate from the optimal O*; the genuine sequential T5..T2 chain; an operationalized multi-dimensional notion of 'reduction' that never equates fewer digits with less information; preservation/fiber/boundary tests; held-out methodology; dataset schema/generator/factor-fidelity tests explicitly required to prevent repeating the old generator's metadata-leak defect; falsification criteria) plus eight stop conditions and a mandatory binary READY-FOR-IMPLEMENTATION / NOT-READY verdict, explicitly forbidding code implementation or dataset generation at this stage.

anchor: Zero_{T_n,Pi}(S_n;R^n) => Adeq(R^{n-1},Q,Pi) as the Zero-boundary hypothesis. I would not formulate it that strongly anymore ... Zero is itself a judgment produced by (D,T,Pi,S).
statement: Rejects a proposed strong 'Zero-boundary hypothesis' (Zero at a reduction step implies adequacy of the next representation) as formulated too strongly, arguing instead that Zero is one observable judgment produced by the underlying tuple (D,T,Pi,S), with an unnamed interaction structure I_{T,Pi}(D,S) as the real open mathematical object -- reframing the research question from 'what does Zero predict?' to 'what structure determines the boundary at which reduction ceases to preserve the contract, of which Zero is one detection mechanism?'

anchor: KR-ZERO discovered empirical constraints on context-dependent eliminability and revealed that relational structure may enter through the transformation/preservation pair. KR-REP-REDUCTION now independently investigates representation reduction ... using the KR-ZERO findings as controlled experimental factors and hypotheses -- not as definitions or conclusions.
statement: Revises the relationship between the two experiment families: rather than 'KR-ZERO discovers eliminability; KR-REP-REDUCTION tests whether Zero predicts adequacy,' the corrected position is that KR-ZERO's findings become controlled experimental factors and hypotheses for KR-REP-REDUCTION, never definitions or conclusions it inherits; elevates the representation carrier (individual element vs subset vs relational structure/hypergraph/rewriting state) to a first-class unresolved research question that must be settled before R5->R2 can be properly designed.

anchor: Adequacy != Contract Realization ... otherwise a representation could look mathematically sufficient while failing the actual preservation/operational contract.
statement: Adopts Adequacy != Contract Realization as a hard experimental rule for KR-REP-REDUCTION, distinguishing T_Adeq(Q) (sufficient information exists) from T_Real(Pi) (the specified operator O actually realizes it, and admissibility holds), so that a mathematically sufficient representation is never conflated with one that actually satisfies the operational contract.

anchor: KR-ZERO: When can source material be eliminated while preserving the contract? KR-REP-REDUCTION: How far can the representation be reduced while retaining inquiry adequacy and contract realization? The bridge is a hypothesis to test, not an established implication.
statement: States the final, precise research-question separation between the two experiment families and explicitly classifies the connecting arrow (Zero_{T_n,Pi} -> candidate elimination -> R^{n-1} -> Adequacy/Realization) as a hypothesis to be tested by KR-REP-REDUCTION, never an established implication inherited from KR-ZERO; freezes a status ledger distinguishing [CORPUS] established facts, [EXP] established mathematical results (H(Q|T)=0 adequacy; H(T|Q)=0 no-excess; hence H(T)=H(Q)+H(T|Q)), [PROP] proposed measures (Excess_Q(T)=H(T|Q); Zero predicting adequacy), and five explicit [OPEN] questions (existence of a general R5->R2 chain; the representation carrier; monotonicity; whether Zero predicts the boundary; whether relational structure in T,Pi predicts reduction difficulty).

anchor: X_Q(R) = H(R|Q) as Q-relative residual representation, with excess representation as an interpretation only when the contract explicitly says those distinctions are unnecessary.
statement: Names the final residual-representation quantity X_Q(R)=H(R|Q) as 'Q-relative residual representation,' explicitly reserving the normatively loaded term 'excess representation' only for cases where the preservation contract itself declares the residual distinctions unnecessary, on the principle that what is unnecessary for one inquiry is not thereby unnecessary for every inquiry (provenance, uncertainty bounds, or lineage may be irrelevant to Q while still required by the broader contract Pi).

anchor: R(Q,Pi) = (D, {R_n}, {T_n}, O, Q, Pi) ... M_n = (A_n, F_n, H_hat(Q|R_n), X_Q(R_n), H_hat(R_n), N_viol,n) ... n* = min{n in {1..5} : Comp_n=1.0 and A_n=1.0 and N_viol,n=0 and H_hat(Q|R_n)=0}.
statement: Presents the fully frozen KR-REP-REDUCTION experimental protocol as the object R(Q,Pi)=(D,{R_n},{T_n},O,Q,Pi) with directional chain D->T5->R5->T4->R4->T3->R3->T2->R2->T1->R1, entropy/size/count recorded independently per level (monotonicity treated as an empirical hypothesis, never assumed), a completeness-declared per-level measurement vector M_n=(A_n,F_n,H_hat(Q|R_n),X_Q(R_n),H_hat(R_n),N_viol,n), the closed-form fiber-violation formula N_viol,n=sum_r [(sum_q c_{r,q})^2 - sum_q c_{r,q}^2]/2, and the boundary definition n*=min{n: Comp_n=1, A_n=1, N_viol,n=0, H_hat(Q|R_n)=0}, with R_{n*} confirmed as the chain-specific preservation boundary only if the next-lower level fails at least one of those conditions.

anchor: The current design does not yet fully test H-RR3 (T-Pi interaction) ... the controlled 2x2 experiment is deferred ... the next useful review is of the actual implementation and its FT-1...FT-7 execution results.
statement: Notes that the frozen protocol design defers the controlled 2x2 (T_extreme/realistic x Pi_extreme/realistic) test of transformation-preservation interaction (hypothesis H-RR3), so the design phase can investigate the reduction boundary and observe an association with Zero but cannot yet establish a general T-Pi interaction law; records that the theoretical/protocol design phase is complete and the next required review step is of the actual implementation's FT-1 through FT-7 execution results, i.e. an experiment run beyond the scope of this file.
